key_insight: The paper introduces a fidelity-based certification framework that can verify adversarial robustness of quantum machine learning models from measurement data and, when the full model is known, compute an optimal robustness bound via semidefinite programming.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path to trustworthy QML on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware by enabling both theoretical guarantees and real-device robustness evaluation.
method: Derive a robustness lower bound from output measurement distributions.
Formulate the optimal bound as a semidefinite program with full model knowledge.
Package the framework into VeriQR for automated QML robustness verification and benchmarking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical validation through the first quantum adversarial robustness benchmark on a 20-qubit superconducting processor.
watch_item: The strongest certification requires full knowledge of the QML model, and real-device measurements may still be affected by noise and hardware imperfections.
paper_title: Verifying Adversarial Robustness in Quantum Machine Learning: from theory to physical validation via a software tool
